To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Spt6 recruits Iws1 to the CTD and that the Iws1:CTD: Spt6 complex facilitates cotranscriptional histone H3 methylation and mRNA export.
Spt6 recruits Iws1 to the CTD to facilitate mRNA export and HYPB/SETD2-mediated histone modification of transcribed genes.
Spt6 and Iws1 form a complex that binds to the CTD of RNAPII and recruits HYPB/Set2, an enzyme that methylates histone H3 on lysine 36 (H3K3me3), to the RNAPIII transcription complex.

the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of specific genes and how the expression of specific groups of genes are coordinated.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of specific genes in eukaryotic cells.
the mechanisms of gene expression, particularly the mechanisms that control the expression of the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), the virus responsible for AIDS.

Iws1 is required for cotranscriptional RNA synthesis and mRNA export as well for HYPB/Set2-mediated H3K36me across active genes.
